chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
Home staging isn't decorating: it's marketing. The goal isn't to please YOUR taste, but to let the largest number of buyers picture themselves there — and to justify a better price, faster.

This guide gives you an express plan, room by room, doable in a weekend and on a small budget. Simple moves with big impact.

Each chapter ends with a lined « My notes » page to check off your tasks, room by room.

chapters.title: The 3 principles that sell
chapters.objective: Understand the logic before moving a single piece of furniture.
chapters.html:
Understand the logic before moving a single piece of furniture.

  1. Declutter: fewer objects = larger, brighter rooms. It's move number 1, free and the most rewarding.
  2. Depersonalize: put away family photos, mementos and strong personal taste so the buyer can imagine THEIR life here.
  3. Neutralize and clean: subdued colors, a thorough cleaning, neutral smells. An immaculate house inspires confidence.

Remember: you're not decorating for yourself, you're preparing a product for the market.

Emilie's tip

If you do only one thing: declutter aggressively. Clear out 30% of your belongings (boxes in the garage or storage). The effect on the perception of space is spectacular and free.

chapters.title: Exterior and entrance: the first impression
chapters.objective: Win the buyer over before they even step inside.
chapters.html:
Win the buyer over before they even step inside.

  • Facade: mowed lawn, trimmed hedges, clear walkway, hidden garbage bins.
  • Front door: clean, working handle, maybe a fresh coat of paint.
  • Interior entrance: clear, bright, welcoming (a mirror, a plant).

The first impression is decided in a few seconds, from the sidewalk: it sets the tone for the whole visit.

Emilie's tip

Take a photo of your facade with your phone: the camera often reveals what the eye no longer notices (clutter, wear). Fix whatever the photo exposes.

chapters.title: Living spaces and kitchen
chapters.html:
Showcase the spaces that sell.

  • Living room: clear the walkways, maximize light, a few neutral touches.
  • Kitchen: nearly empty counters, clean appliances, seals redone if needed.
  • Dining room: a simply set table to suggest conviviality.
  • Light everywhere: working bulbs, open curtains, a bright atmosphere.

The kitchen and light are two decisive factors: put your energy there first.

Emilie's tip

Clear kitchen counters give an immediate impression of space and cleanliness. Put away everything except 1 or 2 decorative objects: it's one of the most effective moves there is.

chapters.title: Bedrooms, bathrooms and finishing touches
chapters.objective: Tend to the intimate spaces and the details.
chapters.html:
Tend to the intimate spaces and the details.

  • Bedrooms: neutral, tidy bedding, clear space under the beds, decluttered closets (they look bigger).
  • Bathrooms: immaculate, clean matching towels, clean seals and fixtures, a neutral smell.
  • Finishing touches: fix anything that squeaks or sticks, air out, a pleasant temperature on showing days.

The details signal a well-maintained house: they reassure the buyer and reduce their attempts to negotiate downward.

Emilie's tip

Partially empty your closets before showings: a half-full closet looks bigger and suggests « plenty of storage ». Buyers always open the doors.

chapters.title: Action plan
chapters.html:
Your next steps, concretely.

This week

  1. Declutter 30% of your objects (boxes to store away).
  2. Nail the first impression: facade and entrance.

Within 30 days

  1. Deep cleaning, small repairs, optimizing the light.
  2. Prepare each room for the photos and the showings.

Next

  1. Have professional photos taken once the house is ready.

chapters.title: Resources & glossary
chapters.html:
• Declutter: remove superfluous objects to visually enlarge the rooms.
  • Depersonalize: neutralize the decor so the buyer can picture themselves.
  • First impression: the perception created right from the sidewalk.
  • Neutralize: subdued colors and a clean, bright atmosphere.
  • Professional photos: a step to do once the house is prepared.
